requirements.text: raise it one notch below the top
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 184 AND priority = 'high'
assumptions: the ticket is CS-0000184 (case 184): the only alert-channel case at Stark Industries (account 8) on a PA-3220 product, on installed product 42 at location 817, Stark Industries Hq - London
the policy's priority list runs critical, high, moderate, low, so one notch below the top is high (seed value moderate)

requirements.text: Move it off the vendor liaison desk to your first second-line specialists of csm support
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 184 AND assignment_group_id = 2
assumptions: the vendor liaison desk is the case's seed group 52 (Vendor Case Liaison_3)
the first second-line group of CSM support is CSM Tier 2 Support (group 2, active), not the suffixed copies 22, 42 and 62
no user is named, so assigned_to is not tested

requirements.text: Set Tonya Stevens as our poc on this ticket
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 184 AND contact_id = 11
assumptions: Tonya Stevens is user 287, whose contact record at Stark Industries is contact 11; the case's contact on the seed is contact 10

requirements.text: Switch the response target to high with no pause and restart its clock
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 2465 AND case_id = 184 AND sla_def_id = 11 AND stage = 'in_progress' AND start_time > '2025-08-27 15:37:25'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (2464 is the highest case_sla_id on the seed); the task creates exactly one SLA link
the high, no-pause response target is SLA Response - High (No Pause) (sla_def 11, response, pause_on_pending 0), not sla_def 2 (SLA Response - High, which pauses)
a running clock is stage in_progress
a restarted clock starts after the replaced response clock, case_sla 367 (SLA Response - Moderate), which started 2025-08-27 15:37:25

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 367 AND sla_def_id = 3 AND stage IN ('in_progress', 'paused')
assumptions: the case's current response target is row 367, SLA Response - Moderate (sla_def 3, paused); switching means it no longer runs as a target, whether deleted or moved to canceled or completed
implied by 'switch', not stated: the request names the new target, and leaving the old one running would give the case two response targets
no listed tool updates or deletes an existing case_sla row; link_new_case_sla only adds one

assumptions: the case's only title or description field is short_description; it must keep its seed value

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 184 AND state <> 'closed'

requirements.text: take the alert ticket about Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 at our headquarters in the UK's capital
requirements.selector: account_id = 8 AND case_id <> 184 AND (product_id IN (128, 140, 152, 164, 176) OR channel = 'alert')
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 8 AND case_id <> 184 AND (product_id IN (128, 140, 152, 164, 176) OR channel = 'alert') AND assignment_group_id IS NOT 2
assumptions: boundary of the description: Stark Industries' other PA-3220 cases (181, 189, 193, 194, 200 on Variant 8 at the London HQ; 195 on Variant 32) are not alerts, and its other alert cases (191, 198) are not on a PA-3220; none may be moved to CSM Tier 2 Support in place of case 184
products 128, 140, 152, 164 and 176 are every PA-3220 product in the seed; Stark Industries has cases only on 140 and 164

disagreement: selector: one pass selects Stark Industries' cases on products 140 and 164 or on the alert channel, the other its cases on all five PA-3220 products without the alert cases; chose the union, since the alert cases 191 and 198 and every PA-3220 variant are both things a loose reading of the description sweeps in, and the union picks the same 8 rows on the seed

disagreement: cells and expected: one pass counts the rows not in group 2 (expected 8), the other the rows in group 2 (expected 0); chose the count of rows not in group 2, which also fails if a neighbouring case is deleted in place of being left alone

requirements.text: Switch the response target to high with no pause
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 184 AND sla_def_id = 2
assumptions: near match: SLA Response - High (sla_def 2) is the high response target that pauses on pending, the one a loose reading of 'high' would pick; it is not the target asked for and may not be linked to the case

Is SLA-High-No-Pause Linked And Running.evidence: start_time is NOT NULL in the schema, so 'start_time IS NOT NULL' holds for every row and cannot show that the clock was restarted, which the request asks for; the requirement tests start_time later than the start of the replaced response clock (case_sla 367, 2025-08-27 15:37:25). Its other cells (case 184, SLA Response - High (No Pause), stage in_progress) are carried unchanged

notes:
The checks read the case by number and the group and SLA definition by name; the requirements read case_id 184, group_id 2 and sla_def_id 11, the same rows on this seed. The acting user, Tonya Stevens (user 287), is a customer contact at Stark Industries whose role alone would not allow reassigning groups or changing SLAs, but the policy has the assistant act with admin responsibilities by default, so the changes are in scope. The resolution target (case_sla 368, SLA Resolution - Moderate (No Pause)) is neither asked to change nor protected, so it is not tested, although the case's priority becomes high. The ending of the old Moderate response target follows from 'switch', but no listed tool can end or delete an existing case_sla row, so an agent may be unable to meet it unless linking the new target ends the old one. The restarted-clock test assumes new case_sla rows take a start time later than the seed's (all seed SLA clocks start on 2025-08-27). breach_time and has_breached on the new row are derived by the server and not tested. The stay against linking SLA Response - High was written with the same query by both passes; it is kept with the case as the selector and the definition as a cell.
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass requires the replaced response target (case_sla 367, SLA Response - Moderate, paused) to stop running, the other sets no requirement on it because the request does not say what becomes of it and no listed tool edits an existing case_sla row; kept because 'switch the response target' asks for the old target to be replaced, not joined, and a requirement with no tool able to write it is still a requirement.
disagreement: value: the boundary stay on Stark Industries' other cases selects products 140 and 164 or the alert channel in one pass and all five PA-3220 products in the other; chose the union, which picks the same 8 rows on the seed and covers both readings of the description.
disagreement: value: the same boundary stay counts rows not in group 2 (expected 8) in one pass and rows in group 2 (expected 0) in the other; chose the count of rows not in group 2, which also fails if a neighbouring case is deleted.
